title: What a pharmacist must write down when a Schedule II prescription is partially filled
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1306.13(a) the stock-shortage partial fill is permissible only if the pharmacist MAKES A NOTATION OF THE QUANTITY SUPPLIED on the face of the written prescription, in the written record of the emergency oral prescription, or in the electronic prescription record. Under 1306.13(b)(5) a REQUEST-BASED partial fill carries its own notation: where the PRESCRIBER requested it the pharmacist notes the quantity dispensed, and where the request came in a consultation the pharmacist also notes 'Authorized by Practitioner to Partial Fill', the practitioner's name, the date and time of the discussion, and the pharmacist's initials; where the PATIENT, a minor's parent or legal guardian, or an adult patient's caregiver named in a medical power of attorney requested it, the pharmacist notes that the named requester 'requested partial fill on [date such request was made]' together with the quantity dispensed. For every request-based partial filling the pharmacy must also maintain a dispensing record carrying the date of each dispensing, the name or initials of the individual who dispensed, and the other information 21 CFR 1306.22(c) requires for Schedule III and IV refills; for electronic prescriptions that information must be LINKED to the electronic controlled substance prescription record.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate can state what the partial-fill record must actually contain, and that the required notation differs by which pathway and which requester produced the partial fill.

authority.name: Partial filling of prescriptions, notation and records

exceptions: The stock-shortage notation under 1306.13(a) is only the quantity supplied; the fuller request-based notations belong to 1306.13(b)(5).
A consultation-authorized partial fill adds the 'Authorized by Practitioner to Partial Fill' notation that a partial fill requested on the face of the prescription does not require.
common_confusions: Treating partial-fill notation as a Massachusetts-only duty when federal law imposes its own notation in every pathway.
Recording only the quantity on a request-based partial fill and omitting the requester and the date of the request.
Forgetting the separate dispensing record that borrows the Schedule III and IV refill data elements.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1306.13(a) and (b)(5) read verbatim in the current eCFR text on 2026-09-10. Added because the GPT-FRESH-B4-SG-REPAIR-V3 audit found SG-CII-LIFECYCLE stated the Massachusetts partial-fill notation duty with no federal counterpart anywhere in the section, and FED-CII-PARTIAL-72H and FED-CII-PARTIAL-PATIENT are both frozen by RELEASED question adjudications.
